source_meta._title: Horses' armor, reins, and bridles experience z-fighting

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.14.2 in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use a Creative-mode world with cheats enabled as the simplest practical environment for executing the supplied summon command. Use keyboard and mouse controls; key names below assume the default bindings. The report specifies no seed, coordinates, resource pack, graphics preset, shader, or dedicated-server requirement.
preconditions: Install or configure a Minecraft: Java Edition installation/profile for Minecraft 1.14.2, the first version listed as affected.
Do not use 23w14a for this reproduction because the report lists it as the fix version rather than an affected version.
Create or load a single-player world in Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled. Creative mode is an execution convenience; the report does not specify a required game mode.
Wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and movement, camera rotation, and chat input respond normally.
Move to a well-lit, open area with enough unobstructed space to stand near and view a horse from the front and sides.
If controls are rebound, use the bindings for Open Chat, Change Perspective, Use Item/Place Block, and Sneak/Dismount in place of the default T, F5, right-click, and Left Shift inputs.

steps.action: Launch the installation/profile configured for Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.14.2, then enter the prepared single-player world.
steps.success_cue: The world is open in Minecraft 1.14.2 and the player can move and rotate the camera normally.

steps.action: Wait at the open test location until nearby chunks and entity rendering have finished loading. Do not begin while the terrain is visibly appearing or input is delayed.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is fully rendered, the frame updates normally, and movement responds without loading pauses.

steps.action: Set the camera to first-person perspective so later F5 perspective changes are deterministic. Press the Change Perspective key repeatedly, if necessary, until the player's own body is not shown in front of the camera.
steps.exact_input: F5 until first-person perspective is active
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the world and the player's full character model is not visible in front of the camera.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat key to open the in-game chat and command input. The command must be run by the player in chat, with the leading slash included.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept text.

steps.action: Enter the report's summon command exactly as supplied, including capitalization, quotation marks, braces, commas, namespace identifiers, count values, and the leading slash. Press Enter once to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a syntax or permission error, and a horse appears at or immediately beside the player's position wearing diamond horse armor and a saddle.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so the player is not holding an item that could perform a different interaction. The hotbar is the row of nine slots along the bottom of the gameplay screen; press the number key corresponding to an empty slot.
steps.exact_input: Press a number key from 1 through 9 corresponding to an empty hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: No held item is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Move a short distance away if the horse spawned intersecting the player, then approach it until the crosshair can be placed on the center of its torso. Release all movement keys before interacting.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D as needed; center the crosshair on the horse's torso
steps.success_cue: The horse is fully visible at close interaction distance, is not obstructed by blocks, and the crosshair rests on its torso.

steps.action: Use the horse once to mount it. With default controls, right-click the horse while the crosshair is on its torso. Do not open the horse inventory or remove its saddle or armor.
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint rises into the riding position and the riding HUD, such as the horse health and jump indicators, confirms that the player is mounted on the horse.

steps.action: Release all movement controls and allow the mounted horse and camera to become stationary before changing perspective.
steps.exact_input: Release W, A, S, D, Space, and sprint controls
steps.success_cue: The mounted horse is not being deliberately moved or made to jump, and the camera is stable enough for close visual inspection.

steps.action: Switch from first-person to rear third-person perspective so the mounted player, horse, saddle, armor, and reins can be viewed externally.
steps.success_cue: The camera is behind the mounted player and the horse's equipped body and head are visible in the same frame.

steps.action: Use the mouse to angle the third-person camera toward the horse's head and upper neck. Frame the reins closely enough that the strips extending between the horse's bridle area and the rider can be inspected. Keep the horse stationary and hold the view until the camera has rendered several stable frames.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to frame the horse's reins; do not press movement keys
steps.success_cue: The reins and their connection near the horse's head and neck are visible and unobstructed in a stable mounted view.

steps.action: Press the Change Perspective key once more to enter front-facing third-person perspective. Angle the camera slightly downward as needed and frame at least one side of the horse's neck directly below the reins. Hold the resulting viewpoint for several stable rendered frames.
steps.exact_input: F5 once, then move the mouse to frame one side of the neck below the reins
steps.success_cue: The camera faces the mounted player and horse, with the armor and the neck surface immediately below at least one rein visible without block obstruction.

steps.action: Dismount the horse while it still has the summoned saddle and diamond horse armor equipped. With default controls, press the Sneak/Dismount key once; do not attack the horse or open its inventory.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing independently beside the horse, while the same horse remains nearby with its saddle and diamond horse armor equipped.

steps.action: Return to first-person perspective. Because the previous view was front-facing third-person, press F5 once under the default perspective cycle. If the perspective cycle differs, continue only until the player's full model is no longer visible in front of the camera.
steps.exact_input: F5 once, or until first-person perspective is active
steps.success_cue: The camera is in first-person perspective and the dismounted horse remains nearby.

steps.action: Move approximately one to three blocks from the horse, turn toward its head, and center the view on the bridle around its face and muzzle. Adjust the angle only enough to keep the bridle, adjacent armor, and both sides of the head unobstructed; then stop moving and hold the view for several stable rendered frames.
steps.exact_input: Use W/A/S/D and the mouse as needed; center the crosshair near the horse's bridle
steps.success_cue: The player is dismounted and stationary at close viewing distance, with the equipped horse's head and bridle centered and clearly visible.

stor.handoff_condition: The horse has just been mounted in step 8 with its summoned saddle and diamond horse armor still equipped. Begin continuous visual observation at this mounted state, retain observation while the executor frames the reins and neck in steps 10 through 12, and continue through the dismount and final bridle framing in steps 13 through 15. The final state is a stationary first-person close view of the dismounted horse's head and bridle.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a required game mode, world seed, coordinates, world type, graphics setting, resource pack, camera perspective, or lighting condition. Creative mode, a fresh open area, and third-person mounted views are practical execution choices rather than report-stated requirements.

The report contains multiple visual inspection transitions: mounting the horse for the reins, framing the neck below the reins, and dismounting for the bridle. Because the output permits only one trigger_step, step 8 is selected as the earliest trigger and observation should continue through the later viewpoints and dismount.

The exact camera distance and viewing angle are not specified. The plan uses stable, unobstructed third-person mounted views and a close first-person dismounted view to operationalize 'look closely' without changing the horse or supplied command.
The summon command is preserved verbatim from the report and was not modified or independently web-verified.

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 using the vanilla client and default vanilla resources, in a local single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. A Superflat world and an elevated stone support are used as practical choices to make the comparator easy to approach from every direction.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, the first version listed as affected in the report.
Disable any resource pack that replaces or modifies redstone comparator block models or textures; use the vanilla resource pack for the model under test.
Use a single-player Creative-mode world with cheats enabled so the comparator and support blocks can be obtained without crafting and Spectator mode can be entered by command.
Keep the test comparator isolated from levers, redstone blocks, powered redstone dust, repeaters, comparators, or other possible sources of redstone input.
Use first-person view. Default keyboard and mouse controls are assumed; use the corresponding bound controls if they have been changed.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start an installation configured for Java Edition 1.15.2. Wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is visible and identifies the running version as 1.15.2.

steps.action: Create a local test world. From the title screen, open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and select the Superflat world type. Confirm the options and create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> World Type: Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: World generation begins with Creative mode and commands enabled.

steps.action: Wait before interacting until the player has spawned, nearby terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world and can move without waiting for terrain generation.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory control, which is E by default, and select the Search Items tab identified by the compass icon.
steps.exact_input: E; then click the Search Items tab
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory search field and searchable item grid are visible.

steps.action: Click the search field, search for stone, and place one stack of the ordinary Stone block into hotbar slot 1. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains Stone.

steps.action: Replace the search text with comparator, locate the item named Redstone Comparator, and place it into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 2 contains a Redstone Comparator while slot 1 still contains Stone.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory using E or Escape and move to an open area with no existing redstone components nearby.
steps.exact_input: E or Escape; then W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The normal first-person world view is visible and there is clear ground available for an isolated support pillar.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1, aim at an exposed top face of the ground, and use the place-block control, which is right-click by default, once to place the first Stone support block.
steps.success_cue: One Stone block has been placed on top of the ground.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the Stone block just placed and right-click once more to add a second Stone block above it, producing a two-block-high isolated pillar.
steps.success_cue: A two-block-high Stone pillar stands in open space with air around its sides.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2, aim at the top face of the upper Stone block, and right-click once to place the Redstone Comparator on the pillar.
steps.success_cue: A Redstone Comparator is resting on top of the Stone pillar.

steps.action: Leave the comparator in the state created by its initial placement. Do not right-click the comparator again, and do not place any redstone power source or input component next to it.
steps.success_cue: The comparator remains isolated, receives no rear or side redstone input, and has not been toggled after placement.

steps.action: Press T to open the in-game chat interface so a game-mode command can be executed.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Enter the Spectator-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted, command feedback identifies Spectator mode, and the player can fly and pass through blocks.

steps.action: Using Spectator flight, approach the comparator from one side. Use W, A, S, and D for horizontal movement, Space to rise, Left Shift to descend, and the mouse to look around. Stop just outside the comparator at approximately the height where its three torch elements emerge from the base.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D; Space; Left Shift; mouse movement
steps.success_cue: The camera is immediately beside the comparator and the three torch elements can be used as spatial reference points.

steps.action: Fly forward through the side of the comparator model. Adjust the camera vertically until its viewpoint is inside the comparator base and below the three torch elements, then pitch the view upward so the underside regions of the torch elements are centered. Use small movement adjustments to avoid passing completely through the model.
steps.exact_input: W or the appropriate horizontal movement key; Space/Left Shift for small vertical adjustments; move the mouse upward to look toward the torch undersides
steps.success_cue: The Spectator camera is clipped inside the unpowered comparator, positioned beneath its torch elements, with the underside regions of those elements centered for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in Spectator mode and the camera has just been positioned inside the isolated, unpowered comparator beneath its three torch elements, looking upward at their underside regions. Begin model-face observation without changing the comparator state or camera position.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, terrain type, support-block arrangement, or comparator orientation. A Superflat Creative world and a two-block-high Stone pillar are practical execution choices that preserve the reported requirement of placing an unpowered comparator while making spectator-camera positioning easier.

The report does not provide exact camera coordinates or viewing angles. The final position must therefore be adjusted based on the rendered model until the camera is inside the comparator base and below the torch elements.
The report does not explicitly specify whether custom resource packs were active. This plan uses vanilla resources because the report identifies the affected vanilla comparator model files.
No external verification was needed because the report supplies the required edition, affected versions, target block state, game mode, and triggering camera action.

source_meta._title: Cullface arguments in cauldrons are excessive

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1 in a new single-player Superflat world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled only to construct and validate the contraption, then change to Survival mode before entering it. Use the default resource pack and do not enable the attached cauldron-fix resource pack or any other pack that replaces the cauldron model.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected Java Edition version 1.17.1, not the fix version 1.18 Pre-release 1 or a newer release.
Ensure no resource pack that changes the cauldron block model is active. In particular, do not install or enable cauldron-interior-fix-21w43a-v1.0.zip from the report.
Create a new single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative, Allow Cheats enabled, and World Type set to Superflat. The report supplies no required seed.
Use default controls or their rebound equivalents: T opens chat, W moves forward, Space controls flight in Creative, and right-click uses a trapdoor or lever.
The commands below are in-game chat commands. Include the leading slash, press Enter after each command, and wait for the command-success message before continuing.

steps.action: From the launcher, start Minecraft Java Edition 1.17.1. At the title screen, open Options -> Resource Packs and ensure that only the built-in default resources are active; then return to the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left title-screen version text identifies Java Edition 1.17.1, and no cauldron-model resource pack is selected.

steps.action: Create the Superflat Creative single-player world described in the preconditions and wait until terrain has rendered and movement and chat respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Superflat world in Creative mode and can execute commands.

steps.action: Press T, enter the foundation command including its leading slash, and press Enter. This creates a stone platform around the fixed test coordinates.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that blocks were filled at the specified location.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to create a three-block-wide approach floor leading toward the cauldron.
steps.success_cue: A raised stone approach floor exists from Z=-4 through Z=-1 at Y=100.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place an empty cauldron at X=0, Y=100, Z=0.
steps.success_cue: An empty cauldron occupies block coordinates 0 100 0 immediately south of the approach floor.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place the low stone ceiling over the final two approach blocks. The one-block-high clearance beneath this ceiling keeps the player in a crawling pose while approaching the cauldron.
steps.success_cue: Stone ceiling blocks occupy 0 102 -2 and 0 102 -1, with a one-block-high passage between the approach floor and ceiling.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place an open top-half oak trapdoor at the north entrance to the low passage.
steps.success_cue: An open, vertically oriented oak trapdoor is visible at 0 101 -3 in front of the low passage.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place a downward-facing sticky piston three blocks above the cauldron.
steps.success_cue: A retracted sticky piston at 0 103 0 points downward toward the cauldron.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place the movable solid block on the sticky piston's face. In this retracted position, it is one block above the position directly touching the cauldron.
steps.success_cue: A stone block occupies 0 102 0; block 0 101 0 directly above the cauldron remains empty.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to place a support block immediately east of the sticky piston.
steps.success_cue: A stone support block occupies 1 103 0 beside the piston.

steps.action: Press T and execute the command to attach an unpowered lever to the underside of the support block. This places the lever above and east of the cauldron where it can be reached from inside.
steps.success_cue: An unpowered ceiling-mounted lever hangs at 1 102 0, immediately east of the movable stone block.

steps.action: Press T and teleport to the centered starting point north of the trapdoor. The final two numbers orient the player south toward the contraption.
steps.success_cue: The player stands centered on the approach at X=0.5 and faces south toward the open trapdoor, low tunnel, and cauldron.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, validate the lever and piston before entering the contraption. If necessary, double-tap Space to fly, move within right-click reach of the ceiling lever, aim at its handle, and right-click it once.
steps.success_cue: The lever turns on, the sticky piston extends downward, and the movable stone block is pushed from 0 102 0 to 0 101 0 directly above the cauldron.

steps.action: Right-click the same lever a second time to reset the mechanism before the actual reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The lever turns off, the sticky piston retracts, the stone block returns to 0 102 0, and the space at 0 101 0 directly above the cauldron is open again.

steps.action: Press T and teleport back to the centered starting point north of the trapdoor.
steps.success_cue: The player is centered on the approach, faces south, and the open trapdoor is directly ahead.

steps.action: Press T and switch to Survival mode before entering the cauldron. This preserves the report's condition that the enclosed cauldron interior is reachable during Survival gameplay.
steps.success_cue: The Survival health, hunger, and hotbar interface is visible, and the player remains at the approach entrance.

steps.action: Hold W to walk directly south until positioned against or within the space of the vertically open trapdoor. Keep the player centered at approximately X=0.5 so the player will align with the narrow center opening of the cauldron.
steps.success_cue: The player is immediately beside the open trapdoor, facing into the one-block-high stone passage.

steps.action: Aim at the oak trapdoor and right-click once to close it over the player's upper body. Do not break the trapdoor.
steps.success_cue: The trapdoor is horizontal in its closed top-half position, the camera lowers, and the player enters the prone crawling pose beneath it.

steps.action: Hold W to crawl south through the one-block-high passage. Continue straight over the centered opening of the cauldron until the player drops into its interior, then release W. Do not move sideways because the cauldron's interior opening is narrow.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary inside the empty cauldron at 0 100 0, below the rim; the low viewpoint is surrounded by the cauldron interior, and the ceiling-mounted lever is above and to the east/right.

steps.action: Without leaving the cauldron, turn the view upward and east toward the ceiling-mounted lever at 1 102 0. Center the crosshair on the lever handle. Do not click until the lever is clearly targeted and within reach.
steps.success_cue: The lever handle is under the crosshair while the player remains inside the cauldron and the piston is still retracted.

steps.action: Right-click the ceiling-mounted lever exactly once, then stop all movement and input as soon as the piston finishes extending.
steps.success_cue: The lever is powered, the sticky piston has completed its downward extension, the stone block now occupies 0 101 0 directly above the cauldron, and the player remains enclosed inside the cauldron.

stor.handoff_condition: The Survival-mode player is inside the cauldron at 0 100 0 immediately after pulling the lever; the piston is fully extended and a solid stone block occupies 0 101 0 directly on top of the cauldron. Begin observation without moving the player, toggling the lever again, or changing the resource pack.
uncertainties: The three screenshot attachments showing the reporter's exact contraption were not included in the supplied report text and could not be recovered from the permitted external sources. The plan therefore uses a minimal deterministic sticky-piston-and-lever contraption that preserves the reported sequence: initiate crawling with a trapdoor, enter the cauldron, and pull a lever to move a solid block directly above it.

The report does not specify the trapdoor material or the type of solid block moved above the cauldron. Oak trapdoor and stone are practical implementation choices and are not asserted as requirements of the bug.

The report does not formally specify a game mode for world construction. Creative mode and cheats are used only to construct and validate the deterministic setup; the player is switched to Survival before performing the reported crawling and lever sequence.
No world seed or original coordinates are supplied. Coordinates around 0 100 0 and a Superflat world are practical choices intended to eliminate terrain and exploration variability.

source_meta._title: Vex texture does not utilize translucency

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w45a in a vanilla single-player world (integrated server). Use Creative mode with commands/cheats enabled for deterministic positioning and command execution. Use the built-in Allay and Vex textures; disable resource packs or other modifications that replace or alter either entity texture.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w45a is installed and selected in the Minecraft Launcher.
A single-player world can be created or opened with commands/cheats enabled.
The executing player has permission to run /summon commands.
No resource pack, shader, or mod that replaces or alters the Allay or Vex texture is active.
There is enough unobstructed space to summon and view two entities at the same height.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 22w45a snapshot installation from the Minecraft Launcher.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running game version as snapshot 22w45a.

steps.action: Create a new single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. A Superflat world may be used to provide a clear viewing area; no particular seed is required by the report.
steps.success_cue: The player enters a world in Creative mode and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait for initial world loading to finish before summoning either entity.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, player movement responds normally, and the loading screen is no longer visible.

steps.action: Move to a clear, well-lit location where blocks, vegetation, and other entities will not obscure the summoned mobs. In Creative mode, double-tap Space to begin flying and position the player a few blocks above the surface so the entities' lower regions can be viewed without ground obstruction.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in an unobstructed area with clear air around the current position.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's Allay summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An Allay is visible one block in the negative X direction from the command execution position and remains stationary because NoAI is set.

steps.action: Without moving away from the summon position, press T again to reopen in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open while the summoned Allay remains present.

steps.action: Enter the report's Vex summon command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A Vex is visible one block in the positive X direction from the command execution position and remains stationary because NoAI is set; both the Allay and Vex are present.

steps.action: Move several blocks away from the two stationary mobs and rotate the camera until the complete Allay and Vex models are visible at the same time. Reposition around the pair as needed because the commands place them along the world's X axis rather than relative to the camera's left and right directions.
steps.success_cue: Both mobs are simultaneously visible, neither model is blocked by the player or terrain, and their lower body regions are large enough on screen to inspect.

steps.action: Center the view on the ragged-looking region at the bottom of each mob and begin a side-by-side visual examination of those corresponding regions. Do not change versions, textures, resource packs, or graphics configuration after positioning the camera.
steps.success_cue: The stationary Allay and Vex are framed together with both bottom ragged-looking regions clearly exposed for the observation subsystem.

stor.handoff_condition: Both NoAI entities have been summoned in snapshot 22w45a, and the camera is now positioned so the ragged-looking bottom regions of the Allay and Vex can be examined side by side. Begin visual observation at this point.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, world type, game mode, lighting condition, camera direction, or graphics setting. Creative mode, a clear well-lit area, and an optional Superflat world are practical choices for deterministic command execution and unobstructed viewing, not stated reproduction requirements.

The report does not explicitly require vanilla resource settings, but texture-altering resource packs, shaders, or mods are excluded so they do not replace or modify the entity textures being compared.

The report's reproduction targets the ragged-looking lower regions of the mobs. Later comments discussing Vex wings describe a potentially separate issue and are therefore not incorporated into these steps.

source_meta._title: Order of rendering translucent block faces fails to update with camera position

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.7.2 in singleplayer, using keyboard and mouse, Creative mode, cheats enabled, no shaders or rendering-mod clients, and a render distance greater than the two-chunk minimum. The deterministic procedure uses the version-compatible 1.7.2 representation of the report's stained-glass Superflat preset.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.7.2; do not select the fix version 24w36a.
Use an unmodified client without OptiFine, Sodium, shaders, or other mods that can replace translucent-block rendering.
Make sure the computer has a working F3 key. On keyboards where F-keys control hardware functions, the Fn key may also need to be held.
Use a render distance above two chunks so that multiple stained-glass chunks around each teleport destination can render.
The test world must be newly generated from the supplied layer arrangement: bedrock, green stained glass, red stained glass, and blue stained glass, from bottom to top.
Do not press F3+T, change video settings, reload chunks, or intentionally move after the final teleport; those actions can alter the rendering state that the observation subsystem needs to inspect.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact release 1.7.2, start it, and wait for the main menu. Do not use the 24w36a fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.7.2.

steps.action: From the main menu, open Options, then Video Settings. Set Render Distance to Normal or Far rather than Tiny, then return to the main menu. This ensures that more than two chunks are available around the teleport destinations.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is visible again and Render Distance is set above the minimum two-chunk setting.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Click the Game Mode button until it displays Game Mode: Creative. Creative mode is needed to perform the report's flying step without building anything.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Select More World Options. Turn Allow Cheats ON so that both teleport commands can be run. Cycle World Type until Superflat is selected, and turn Generate Structures OFF to keep the glass plane unobstructed.
steps.success_cue: Allow Cheats is ON, World Type is Superflat, and Generate Structures is OFF.

steps.action: With Superflat selected, click Customize, then click Presets. Select all text in the preset text box, delete it, and enter the provided 1.7.2-compatible preset exactly. This is the historical numeric-ID equivalent of the report's named-ID preset: bedrock at the bottom, then green stained glass, red stained glass, and blue stained glass. In this syntax, 7 is bedrock, 95 is stained glass, and metadata 13, 14, and 11 select green, red, and blue respectively. Minecraft 1.7.2 requires the older preset format and does not have the report's the_void biome. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/%D0%A1%D1%83%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The preset text box contains exactly "2;7,95:13,95:14,95:11;1;" with no spaces or additional characters.

steps.action: Click Use Preset, then click Done to return to the main world-creation screen. Click Create New World.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins generating and loading the new world.

steps.action: Wait without issuing commands until world generation finishes, the surrounding terrain is rendered, and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on an uninterrupted flat blue stained-glass surface; the red and green stained-glass layers are directly beneath it, and nearby chunks have finished rendering.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight by quickly pressing the Jump control twice; the default input is a double-tap of Space.
steps.success_cue: The player is flying and remains suspended instead of falling back onto the blue glass.

steps.action: Press F3 to display the debug overlay. Hold the Jump control, default Space, to ascend until the displayed Y coordinate is approximately 10 blocks above the glass surface. With this four-layer preset, a player initially stands at about Y=4, so a target near Y=14 is suitable. Release Space when that height is reached, then press F3 again to hide the overlay.
steps.exact_input: F3; hold Space until approximately Y=14; release Space; F3
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering approximately ten blocks above the blue stained-glass surface and is no longer ascending.

steps.action: Press T once to open the in-game chat input. The command must be executed in the player chat, not in the launcher or an external console.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Type the report's first teleport command exactly, including the leading slash, then press Enter. The command moves the nearest player to X=100 and Z=100, preserves the current Y coordinate through the relative "~" argument, and sets camera yaw to 135 and pitch to 45.
steps.success_cue: The chat closes, the teleport completes, and the player is hovering near X=100 and Z=100 while looking in the command-specified direction.

steps.action: Do not continue immediately. Keep movement inputs released and wait until the stained-glass terrain around X=100, Z=100 has rendered across multiple chunks and the game responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Multiple surrounding stained-glass chunks are visible, loading activity has settled, and the client is responsive.

steps.action: Reload client resources using the report's debug shortcut: hold F3, tap T once while F3 remains held, then release both keys. On a keyboard with media-function F-keys, hold Fn as needed. F3+T reloads client resources, including textures and models. ([ja.minecraft.wiki](https://ja.minecraft.wiki/w/%E3%83%87%E3%83%90%E3%83%83%E3%82%B0%E7%94%BB%E9%9D%A2?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The client briefly pauses or redraws as resources reload, then returns to the world view.

steps.action: After the F3+T reload, keep all movement inputs released and wait until the surrounding stained-glass chunks have rendered again and the game responds normally. Do not move the camera or player during this wait unless required to restore game-window focus.
steps.success_cue: The player remains near X=100, Z=100 at the same height and orientation, multiple glass chunks are rendered, and the client is responsive.

steps.action: Press T once to reopen the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready for the second teleport command.

steps.action: Type the report's second teleport command exactly, including the leading slash, then press Enter. The command moves the nearest player to X=0 and Z=0, preserves the current Y coordinate, and sets yaw to -45 and pitch to 45. Executing this command is the reproduction trigger.
steps.success_cue: The chat closes and the player is teleported back near X=0 and Z=0 at the preserved height and command-specified camera orientation.

steps.action: Immediately release all movement and camera controls. Without pressing F3+T, changing video settings, or deliberately moving, wait only until the stained-glass terrain at the destination is rendered sufficiently for visual inspection. Hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the destination view is available.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near X=0 and Z=0, hovering above the glass at yaw -45 and pitch 45, and multiple destination chunks are available for inspection without any post-teleport movement or rendering reset.

stor.handoff_condition: The second teleport has just placed the stationary player near X=0 and Z=0 at the preserved flight height, with yaw -45 and pitch 45. Destination glass chunks are visible, and no movement, resource reload, chunk reload, or video-setting change has been performed after the teleport. Begin inspecting the translucent stained-glass layers now.
uncertainties: The report supplies the modern preset "minecraft:bedrock,minecraft:green_stained_glass,minecraft:red_stained_glass,minecraft:blue_stained_glass;minecraft:the_void", but the required first affected version, Minecraft 1.7.2, predates that named-ID preset format and predates the Void biome. The plan therefore uses the verified historical equivalent "2;7,95:13,95:14,95:11;1;", substituting the available plains biome while preserving the exact block layers and their order. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/%D0%A1%D1%83%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BF%D0%BB%D0%BE%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%BE%D1%81%D1%82%D1%8C?utm_source=openai))
The report does not specify a world seed. No seed is selected because the custom Superflat layer arrangement is uniform and deterministic.

The report says to fly up approximately ten blocks and explicitly notes that the exact amount does not matter much. The target of approximately Y=14 assumes the player begins standing above the four generated layers near Y=4.

The report does not prescribe an exact render distance, but one report comment states that the issue could not be reproduced at a render distance of two chunks and could be reproduced above that setting. Normal or Far is selected as a deterministic practical setting for Minecraft 1.7.2.

The report's supplied reproduction was rewritten long after Minecraft 1.7.2. Although its layer arrangement can be translated to the older Superflat format, the report does not explicitly confirm the rewritten command sequence against the 1.7.2 user interface.
